components.name: wireguard
components._note: A MikroTik RouterOS image carries exactly this. wireguard:wireguard is a real product in the NVD index, with rows at 0.5.3; only the version kept the two apart. The CPE is syft's construction from the module name, and the 1.0.0 is the module's own modinfo field.

components.name: zlib
components._note: zlib is on the CPE name whitelist, so this one also proves the name map cannot hand an identifier back to a module after the module rule withholds one.

components.name: busybox
components._note: Not a kernel module. Enrichment must still reach it, or the rule has been written too widely.

components.name: linux_kernel
components._note: The kernel the modules belong to, reported on its own. This is why dropping the modules' identifiers loses nothing: the thing that has a real CPE and a real version is here.
